rules: Top 3 in the Pacific or a wild card

headings.leadersBlurb: These two lead the West divisions. Everyone else is chasing the other six berths.
headings.pathsBlurb: Finish top three in the Pacific, or be one of the two best remaining teams in the West.
headings.footer: Updated from the NHL’s public API. Not affiliated with the NHL or the Oilers.
headings.footerTiny: Eight teams in the conference qualify: the top three in each division and two wild cards. A regulation win and an overtime win are both two points. The playoff percentage is a season simulation from points percentage and home ice. It is not a betting line.
headings.conclusion: The Edmonton Oilers have been mathematically eliminated from the Stanley Cup playoffs.
headings.rootingBlurb: Win odds use the same points model as the playoff card. Not a betting line, and not a live in-game number.

narrative.headline: In the field
narrative.blurb: The Oilers are in through the Pacific top three. The cushion is 3 up. Every remaining point is about staying there.

primary.label: Points up on the cut line

third.label: Magic number to clinch
third.sub: Points to lock Pacific top three
third.note: 162 more points guarantees Pacific top three, no matter how the rest of the West finishes. A win is worth 2. An overtime loss still hands the other team a point.

playoffOdds.note: Each remaining game is simulated from points percentage, shrunk toward .500, with a home-ice bump. About 23% of games go past regulation and give the loser a point. Not a betting line.

kpis.label: ROW
kpis.hint: Regulation plus overtime wins. Shootout wins do not count.

kpis.label: Schedule
kpis.hint: Average opponent strength still on the board

wildcard.title: West wild card
wildcard.detail: A wild card is not required. The Oilers are already inside the division's top three.
